caption:
बॉस! क्या सच में एक और रामायण की कोई जरूरत थी?
प्रोजेक्ट के प्रोड्यूसर नमित मल्होत्रा का कहना है कि भारत में कई लोग यही सवाल पूछ रहे हैं।
फिल्ममेकर ने पीटीआई को बताया कि वे वैसी कहानी दिखाना चाहते हैं जैसी कभी नहीं देखी गई।
नमित मल्होत्रा का दावा है कि इसे अवतार, द ओडिसी या एवेंजर्स जैसी फिल्मों की टक्कर का बनाया जा रहा है।
मंगलवार को मुंबई में फिल्म की खास स्क्रीनिंग हुई, जिसमें कास्ट और क्रू शामिल हुए।
इस फिल्म के डायरेक्टर नितेश तिवारी हैं और बजट करीब 4000 करोड़ रुपये बताया गया है।
फिल्म में रणबीर कपूर भगवान राम, साई पल्लवी सीता और यश रावण के रोल में नजर आएंगे।
पहला पार्ट 5 नवंबर 2026 को और दूसरा पार्ट दिवाली 2027 को रिलीज होगा।
सोनी पिक्चर्स भारत के बाहर ग्लोबल डिस्ट्रीब्यूशन देखेगी और फिल्म 70,000 स्क्रीन पर रिलीज होगी।
क्या आपको भी लगता है कि हॉलीवुड जैसी भव्यता भारतीय सिनेमा में आनी चाहिए?

ctx.title: Ramayana producer Namit Malhotra admits many in India ask why are they making another adaptation, compares film to Avatar, The Odyssey
ctx.summary: Namit Malhotra, producer of Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana, has addressed the need for another adaptation of the epic.
ctx.text:
Ramayana producer Namit Malhotra has admitted that many in India are wondering what the need is for another adaptation of the epic. The filmmaker has talked about the film's scale and ambition, saying it tells its story on a scale never seen before.
Directed by Nitesh Tiwari , Ramayana is the biggest Indian film in terms of scale and budget. After its world premiere in Los Angeles last week, Ramayana held a special screening in Mumbai on Tuesday, attended by the cast and crew, as well as members of the film fraternity.
There, Namit spoke to news agency PTI about what he hopes to achieve with the film. "In India, there are a lot of questions like, 'Why are they making the Ramayana when there have been so many Ramayanas? We already know the story.' And I'm like, 'Listen, we're making it because we want to show you the version of this story that you've never seen.' No television show, no street play, no Ram Leela has ever shown you the Ramayana on this scale and with this spectacle that we are making...Much like an Avatar or an Avengers movie or think about Spider-Man or The Odyssey. We're putting Ramayana right up there next to all of those spectacles," Namit Malhotra told PTI.
Ramayana, made on a reported budget of ₹ 4000 crore, is one of the most expensive film productions in the world, not just in India. With VFX from eight-time Oscar-winning studio DNEG, it is being marketed as India's first film equivalent of Hollywood blockbusters. For its global release, the makers have partnered with Sony Pictures, which is giving it the widest release for any Indian film - in 70,000 screens.
Talking about the film's global ambitions, Namit added, “If you think about the West, they are the most potent audience for anything that's got a grand epic spectacle. And that's just not how Indian films have been made. So while India makes terrific Indian movies, whether it is 'Baahubali', 'Dhurandhar', or any of the big, super-duper hit films, they are not spectacles the way Hollywood thinks of spectacles. We are first trying to narrow that gap down and saying, 'If you can do it, we can do it too.' There's no reason for us to have any discrepancy. So, every person in Hollywood should acknowledge that India can also do something as good, if not bigger, than what they do.”
Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit's Prime Focus and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Yash as Ravana. The first part is scheduled for worldwide release on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2027. The films will release in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.
Sony Pictures will handle global distribution, excluding India, while Dharma Productions will distribute the film in the Hindi-speaking market. The film is also planned for a worldwide IMAX release.
Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well.

A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism.

Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic.
